title: I’ve been building a 2v2 monster battler. Is the combat actually fun?
author: Busy-Landscape-7657
selftext:
**Game Title:** Legacy Beasts  
**Playable Link:** https://legacy-beasts-combat.replit.app/  
**Platform:** Browser (PC & Mobile)  
**Description:**  
I’ve been building **Legacy Beasts**, a 2v2 turn-based monster battler that’s currently in the prototype/alpha stage.  
The current build includes:  
10 unique beasts with different roles and abilities  
Team building and strategic swapping  
Energy and Ultimate system  
AI battles  
Online PvP through private room codes  
Mobile and PC browser support (no download required)  
Right now I’m focused on one thing: **making the combat as fun and strategic as possible** before expanding into progression, more monsters, story, and other features.  
I’d really appreciate any honest feedback, especially on the gameplay.  
Some questions:  
Was the combat fun?  
Did the energy/ultimate system make sense?  
Did swapping feel meaningful?  
Which beast felt the strongest?  
Which beast felt the weakest?  
Was there anything confusing or frustrating?  
Would you play another match? If not, why?  
This is still an early prototype, so I’m looking for gameplay feedback more than polished visuals. Thanks to anyone who takes the time to try it out!

comments.author: Redditry199
comments.body:
No.

Attack names are boring.

The options arent really tactical easy to ultimate attack, and 2 defend buttons.

I started again added elements nothing really feels different.

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body: Thanks for taking the time to play it. I appreciate the honest feedback. I’m especially interested in hearing more about what made the decisions feel untactical to you. Was there a particular action or mechanic that felt unnecessary?

replies.author: Redditry199
replies.body: Whats the point of different beasts if all do the same attack in different lazy Basic to Ultimate scale? You didnt really put any thought or care into this man.

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body:
Just to reiterate, this is a **combat prototype**. My focus right now is testing whether the gameplay is fun before I build out the full game.  
Each beast has:  
Unique stats  
A passive ability  
Active abilities  
Different elemental interactions  
You can view every beast’s abilities and stats in the in-game Wiki if you’d like to dive deeper.  
The Basic, Heavy, and Ultimate actions represent different **energy costs and attack speeds** rather than every beast having completely different move sets. The strategy comes from combining each beast’s passive, active abilities, stats, elemental matchups, and team composition.  
If anyone wants to 1v1 me live, I’ll be on standby. I’d love to play some matches and hear your feedback afterward.

replies.author: Smilysis
replies.body:
The whole combat still feals lazy and boring, sorry

I suggest using gameplay formulas like persona, pokemon and etc to make it more engaging.

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body:
Thanks for giving it a try. This build is intentionally a combat prototype, so my main focus right now is testing whether the strategy and decision-making are fun before I spend time building out the presentation.  
The long-term goal is definitely more polished visuals, animations, and overall battle spectacle, but I don’t want to polish a combat system until I’m confident the gameplay itself is worth building on.  
I appreciate the feedback either way.

replies.author: Terra711
replies.body:
You did the right thing prototyping early. 

I don't like the music, it adds urgency as if its trying to pressurise me. That's the wrong feel in a turn based game. The whole point of it being turn based is you have time to think, glad I could mute it.

In terms of actual combat, it felt slow and dull. If you open with an ultimate you have little to do after. Creatures felt all the same despite there being some customization. The whole system felt convoluted and unintuitive. 

To answer your questions:

Was the combat fun? No  


Did the energy/ultimate system make sense? You have 10 energy, you use it. Get 1 back each turn? Didn't know if there was any more.  


Did swapping feel meaningful? Nope.   


Which beast felt the strongest? 

They all felt the same. Everything dies in two ultimate so I just used the fastest to kill enemy first.  


Which beast felt the weakest? See above.   


Was there anything confusing or frustrating? 

Whole experience was not fun. Pokemon leans into type advantage. You don't justify why you have 2 vs 1 or 3 or 4. The symmetrical resolution is basically just gambling.   


Would you play another match? If not, why? 

Nope. Its not about polish, it's the whole system. You have nothing that feels good. Brave and Default brought something fresh to the genre. You can either focus on making a polished version of systems that are know to work or play more games in the genre to find ideas. The one thing about your creatures, they're generic. They have no character and in monster battling games, having affinity for your creatures is paramount.

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body:
Thanks for taking the time to write all of this. I genuinely appreciate the detailed feedback.  
My goal with this build was to prototype the combat systems first, so it’s really helpful to hear how a first-time player experienced them. I’ll definitely think about your points regarding creature identity, swapping, pacing, and the energy system.  
Thanks again for giving it a shot.

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body:
Combat is one element of gameplay.   
This prototype tests the   
battle system specifically before building   
the full game. overworld, collecting,   
story and progression come later.

comments.author: Trick_Mention_8687
comments.body: How did u set up the multiplayer? Or is that just a placeholder?

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body: It’s fully functional. There’s local PvP on the same device and online PvP through hosted rooms with a room code. I built the prototype around human-vs-human matches because that’s where I think the combat shines. If you’d like to try it with someone, I’d love to hear what you think.

replies.author: Trick_Mention_8687
replies.body: I’ll tell my brother to hop in with me in the afternoon as he’s into turn based games a lot and will give better feedback. Can I ask what method did u use for the room code? As in host or dedicated server etc? How much does it cost?

replies.author: Busy-Landscape-7657
replies.body:
I used WebSockets for real time connection   
and a hosted server for the room codes.   
Built it on Replit core plan which keeps it always on.
